tool_input.content:
Incident: HighErrorRate alert on shop namespace (aurora-lab on-prem cluster, kind-aurora-lab / cluster_id kubeconfig-bf223c2bda6f7755). frontend pods returned 502 on /api/* while ALL pods reported Running/Ready.

Root cause: `api` Service's live `spec.selector` was `app: api-v2`, diverging from its own `kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration` annotation (`app: api`) — i.e. someone/something ran an out-of-band `kubectl patch/edit` on the Service that bypassed the manifest apply flow. Actual `api` Deployment pods carry label `app=api`, so zero pods matched the Service selector → `kubectl get ep api` showed `<none>` → kube-proxy had no backend to DNAT to → ClusterIP connections got "Connection refused" → nginx frontend returned 502 for every /api/ request.

**Why this is tricky:** "All pods Running" looks healthy and misleads toward blaming app code or resources. The actual break is at the Service/Endpoints routing layer, invisible unless you check `kubectl get svc,ep -n NAMESPACE` and compare Service selector vs pod labels.

**How to apply / diagnostic checklist for 5xx + all-pods-Running in this cluster:**
1. `kubectl get svc,ep -n <ns>` — look for any Service with empty ENDPOINTS despite Ready pods.
2. `kubectl get svc <name> -o yaml` — compare live `spec.selector` to the `last-applied-configuration` annotation; a mismatch indicates manual drift.
3. `kubectl get pods -n <ns> --show-labels` — confirm which label pods actually carry.
4. Check downstream caller's logs (e.g. nginx frontend) for `connect() failed (111: Connection refused)` to the ClusterIP — this confirms the symptom is live, not theoretical.
5. Fix: `kubectl patch svc <name> -n <ns> -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"<correct-label>"}}}'` to realign selector with actual pod labels (verify no intentional canary deployment exists first via `kubectl get deployments -o wide` and `kubectl get pods -l app=<new-label>` across all namespaces).

No prior incidents found for "shop" and no relevant memory. Cluster identified: kind-aurora-lab (cluster_id: kubeconfig-bf223c2bda6f7755). 

Hypothesis: Since all pods are "Running" but 5xx errors occur, this points to an application-layer issue (bad config, broken dependency connection, or backend service failure) rather than a pod crash. Let's check pods, services, and events in the shop namespace.

Key finding: endpoints/api shows <none> even though the api pods now report 1/1 Running/Ready. This is a service/selector mismatch, not a pod crash — matches "all pods are Running" but 5xx errors (frontend's calls to api:8080 have nowhere to route). Let's verify by comparing the Service selector to the pod labels, and check frontend logs for the actual 5xx errors.

Found the mismatch: Service api's live selector is app: api-v2, but the last-applied-configuration annotation (the originally intended manifest) shows selector app: api. All actual pods carry label app=api. This selector drift means zero pods match the service, confirmed by endpoints/api = <none>. Let's confirm the frontend is actually seeing failures hitting this api service (not just a theoretical issue), and check nginx config for the upstream reference.

Summary: Frontend Pod Logs (frontend-76d98597b9-fgsvz in shop namespace)

Command: kubectl logs frontend-76d98597b9-fgsvz -n shop --tail=100 (succeeded, exit code 0)

Key Findings:

Nginx startup: The frontend container is an nginx (v1.27.5, Alpine-based) reverse proxy that started successfully at 17:03:50, launching 10 worker processes. A benign warning noted it couldn't modify /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf due to a read-only filesystem.

Health checks: Kubernetes liveness/readiness probes (GET /healthz) are consistently returning 200 OK every ~5 seconds throughout the log — the pod itself is healthy.

Critical Issue — Backend Connectivity Failure:
   - The first request to /api/items at 17:03:55 succeeded (200 OK).
   - Starting at 17:03:59, all subsequent /api/items requests fail with 502 Bad Gateway.
   - Root cause: nginx repeatedly logs connect() failed (111: Connection refused) while connecting to upstream targeting http://10.96.250.20:8080/items.
   - This pattern repeats continuously (every ~2-10 seconds) through the end of the log (17:05:26), indicating a persistent, ongoing outage — not a transient blip.

Traffic source: Requests to /api/items originate from client IP 10.244.2.121 using a Wget user agent (likely an automated test/monitoring script repeatedly polling the endpoint).

Diagnosis: The frontend/nginx proxy is functioning correctly, but the backend service at 10.96.250.20:8080 (likely a Kubernetes ClusterIP service for an "items" API) is refusing connections — suggesting the backend pod(s) are down, crashed, not listening on port 8080, or the service has no healthy endpoints. 

Recommended next steps: Investigate the backend service/deployment behind 10.96.250.20:8080 (check pod status, logs, and endpoints for the service associated with this ClusterIP) to determine why it's refusing connections.

Health checks (/healthz) from kube-probe continue succeeding (200 OK) every 5 seconds, indicating the frontend pod itself is healthy — only its connection to the upstream backend service at 10.96.250.20:8080 is broken.

Root Cause Indication: The backend service (likely a Kubernetes Service ClusterIP at 10.96.250.20:8080) is refusing connections, suggesting the backend pod(s) behind that service are down, crashed, not listening on port 8080, or the service/endpoint configuration is misconfigured. 

Next steps suggested: Investigate the backend pod/service associated with ClusterIP 10.96.250.20:8080 (likely an "items" or "api" service in the shop namespace) — check pod status, logs, and endpoints to determine why connections are being refused.
One more check — verify there's no api-v2 deployment anywhere that this selector was meant to target (to rule out an in-flight canary cutover vs. accidental drift), then finalize.

Investigation Summary

Alert: HighErrorRate — frontend /api/ requests in namespace shop failing with 5xx, pods all Running.

Hypothesis trail
Checked list_incidents/memory for prior "shop" incidents → none found, no stale conclusion to disprove.
All 7 pods in shop are Running/1/1 Ready, 0 restarts — ruled out pod crash/OOM/resource exhaustion as cause.
kubectl get svc,ep -n shop showed endpoints/api = <none> despite 2 healthy api pods → hypothesis: Service/Deployment selector mismatch.
kubectl get svc api -o yaml: live spec.selector = app: api-v2, but the last-applied-configuration annotation (the originally applied manifest) shows selector app: api. This divergence between annotation and live spec is the signature of an out-of-band kubectl edit/patch that bypassed the normal apply flow.
kubectl get pods -l app=api --show-labels: both api pods carry label app=api (not app=api-v2) → confirms zero pods match the Service selector, explaining the empty Endpoints object.
Ruled out "intentional canary/cutover to api-v2": kubectl get deployments -o wide shows only one api Deployment (selector app=api, 2/2 ready); kubectl get pods -A -l app=api-v2 returned nothing cluster-wide. There is no api-v2 workload anywhere — this is pure configuration drift, not a blue-green rollout in progress.
Direct evidence of the symptom actively occurring right now: frontend nginx logs (both replicas) show continuous 502 responses to /api/items, e.g.:
   2026/10/02 17:05:40 [error] ... connect() failed (111: Connection refused) while connecting to upstream ... upstream: "http://10.96.250.20:8080/items" followed by "GET /api/items HTTP/1.1" 502 157. This repeats every few seconds from 17:03:57 through 17:05:40 (the most recent log line), i.e. is ongoing at investigation time. 10.96.250.20 is the api Service ClusterIP — kube-proxy returns "connection refused" because the Service has no backend Endpoints to DNAT to.

Root Cause — CONFIRMED
The api Service's selector was changed from app: api to a

Conclusion

Root cause (CONFIRMED): The api Service in namespace shop has spec.selector: {app: api-v2}, but the only running api pods carry label app=api. This mismatch leaves the Service with zero Endpoints, so every proxy request from frontend to http://api:8080 is refused at the ClusterIP by kube-proxy, which nginx surfaces as 502 to clients hitting /api/*. Confirmed by live, ongoing nginx error logs (connect() failed (111: Connection refused) → 502 on /api/items, timestamps through 17:05:40) — not a theoretical issue, actively reproducing. No api-v2 Deployment or pods exist anywhere in the cluster, ruling out an in-progress canary cutover; this is unexplained configuration drift (the Service's own last-applied-configuration annotation says the intended selector is app: api).

Ruled out: Pod crashes, OOM, resource exhaustion (0 restarts, all 1/1 Ready), and intentional blue/green rollout (no api-v2 workload exists).

Fix (validated, not executed — read-only session):
``
kubectl patch svc api -n shop -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"api"}}}'
`
Validated: pods with label app=api are healthy/Ready (2/2) and will immediately populate Endpoints once the selector is corrected. Risk: low. Undo: re-patch selector to app: api-v2 (reverts to current broken state).

Saved this failure signature to memory (learned: shop namespace: 5xx with all pods Running = Service selector drift`) for faster triage next time this pattern recurs.
